questions.title: Letter grade with if-else
questions.prompt:
Write a function `getGrade(score)` that returns a letter grade using an **if / else if / else** statement:

- 90 or more: `"A"` · 80–89: `"B"` · 70–79: `"C"` · 60–69: `"D"` · below 60: `"F"`
hints: Check the highest range first; then each else if only needs a lower bound.

tests.name: Boundaries 90, 80, 70, 60 give A, B, C, D
89 is B, 59 is F, 100 is A

questions.title: Relational and logical operators
questions.prompt: Write a function `canRent(age, hasLicense)` that returns `true` only when the age is **between 25 and 75 inclusive** **and** `hasLicense` is true. Use the relational operators and the logical operators `&&` / `||` (or `!`) — no if statement needed.
questions.solution: const canRent = (age, hasLicense) => age >= 25 && age <= 75 && hasLicense === true;

tests.name: 25 and 75 with a license are allowed
tests.code: return canRent(25, true) === true && canRent(75, true) === true;

tests.name: 24 and 76 are not allowed
tests.code: return canRent(24, true) === false && canRent(76, true) === false;

questions.title: while loop: doubling
questions.prompt:
Starting with `let value = 1;`, use a **while** loop to keep doubling `value` until it is **greater than 1000**. Count how many times you doubled it in a variable named `doublings`.

(The answer is `value` = 1024 and `doublings` = 10.)

questions.title: do-while loop
questions.prompt: The array `entries` holds values a user typed, in order. Use a **do-while** loop to read entries (starting at index 0) until you find the first one that `parseInt()` turns into a number from **1 to 10**. Store that number in `choice` and the number of entries you read in `tries`.
hints: A do-while loop always runs its body at least once; the condition is checked at the end.
Keep looping while the value is NaN, below 1 or above 10.

questions.title: for loop: factorial
questions.prompt: Write a function `factorial(n)` that uses a **for** loop to return n! (n × (n−1) × … × 1). `factorial(0)` and `factorial(1)` are both 1.
hints: Start a result at 1 and multiply by each number from 2 to n.

tests.name: factorial(10) is 3628800 and a for loop is used

questions.title: Future Value
questions.prompt:
Like the chapter's Future Value application, write a function `futureValue(investment, rate, years)` where `rate` is a yearly percentage (e.g. 5 for 5%). Use a **for** loop that adds a year's interest each year. Return the result **rounded to 2 decimals as a number**.

```
futureValue(10000, 5, 10)   // 16288.95
```
hints: Number(value.toFixed(2)) rounds and keeps it a number.

questions.title: Create and fill an array
questions.prompt:
1. Create an **empty** array named `scores`.
2. Add the scores 85, 92 and 78 to it, using the array's `length` property as the index (`scores[scores.length] = …`), as shown in the chapter.
3. Use a **for** loop with an index to calculate `total`, and then `average` (total ÷ number of scores).
hints: let total = 0; for (let i = 0; i < scores.length; i++) { total += scores[i]; }

questions.title: for-of and for-in loops
questions.prompt:
Given the `names` array:

1. Use a **for-of** loop to build a new array `upper` holding each name in uppercase.
2. Use a **for-in** loop to log each element with its index, like `0: ann`, `1: bo`, `2: cy`.
hints: for (const name of names) gives each value.
for (const i in names) gives each index (as a string).

questions.title: FizzBuzz into an array
questions.prompt: Use a loop from 1 to 15 to fill an array named `results`: for each number, add `"FizzBuzz"` if it's divisible by 3 **and** 5, `"Fizz"` if only by 3, `"Buzz"` if only by 5, and otherwise the number itself.
hints: n % 3 === 0 means divisible by 3. Check the "both" case first.

tests.name: Items 3, 5 and 15 are Fizz, Buzz, FizzBuzz

questions.title: Enhanced Test Scores with validation
questions.prompt: The array `entries` holds text a user typed into `prompt()`. Like the enhanced Test Scores application, loop through them and keep only **valid** scores (numbers from 0 to 100) in a new array `scores`, skipping the rest. Then display `Scores: 88, 100, 0 — Average: 63` in `#result`, with the average rounded to a whole number with `Math.round()`.

setup.css: body { font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; padding: 1em; }

hints: parseInt each entry and check isNaN, < 0 and > 100.

tests.name: scores is [88, 100, 0]
tests.code: return Array.isArray(scores) && scores.length === 3 && scores[0] === 88 && scores[1] === 100 && scores[2] === 0;

tests.name: The page shows the scores and average
